Information about scholarships
List of resources for finding scholarships in France
http://www.campusfrance.org/fr
– always fresh and up-to-date scholarship program offers. Convenient categorization at
http://campusbourses.campusfrance.org/fria/bourse/#/catalog
makes the search intuitively easy.
Scholarships of the Île-de-France region
https://www.iledefrance.fr/education-recherche
https://www.abg.asso.fr/
– a convenient resource for finding Master’s, PhD, and Postdoc programs. Mostly features vacancies from French universities, but also from other countries – Belgium, Germany, etc.
http://formation.sciences-po.fr/en/contenu/the-emile-boutmy-scholarship
– Émile Boutmy Scholarship for Bachelor’s and Master’s students.
You can also find something interesting and useful about studying in France by downloading this
presentation
, kindly provided by Oksana Lando, coordinator of French Government Scholarships.
List of resources for finding scholarships from Nimechchina
https://www.boell.de/en/scholarships/scholarships.html
– The Heinrich Böll Foundation grants scholarships for applicants from all countries and fields of study.
https://www.daad-ukraine.org/uk/
– this site offers a wide range of programs for representatives of all specialties.
https://www.study-in.de/en/
and
https://www.studying-in-germany.org/
– portals about studying and scholarships in Germany.
https://www.study-in-bavaria.de/
– information about studying and receiving scholarships in Bavaria.
http://www.deutschlandstipendium.de
– scholarships for international students in all fields of study.
http://www.mystipendium.de/
– a convenient scholarship search resource.
http://www.kas.de/wf/en/71.14301/
– scholarships for Master’s, PhD studies and scientific research.
https://www.rosalux.de/en/foundation/studienwerk
– Rosa-Luxemburg-Stiftung, another foundation that can fund studies in Germany.
https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/web/programme-nach-zielgruppen.html
– Alexander-von-Humboldt Foundation. A vast range of scholarships depending on the target audience.
http://www.copernicus-stipendium.de
– This scholarship may be of interest to those who are currently students in one of the CIS countries and are considering studying one semester in Germany in one of three cities – Berlin, Hamburg, or Munich.
https://www.fes.de/de/
– Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung. This foundation offers various scholarship programs for study funding.
https://www.study-in.de/en/plan-your-studies/find-programme-and-university
– will help you find a study program and university.
https://www.uni-weimar.de/en/university/research-and-art/young-researchers/scholarships-and-funding/scholarship-databases/
– Several databases with information about scholarships for studying in Germany.
Deutschlandstipendium
– an opportunity to finance your study expenses in Germany. The scholarship is funded 50% by sponsoring companies (Bosch, SAP, BASF), and 50% by the federal budget.
List of resources for finding scholarships in Canada
https://www.educanada.ca/index.aspx?lang=eng
– internships, student reviews, work after graduation, living costs, program search, visas, and everything about student life in Canada!
http://www.cicic.ca/857/Study/index.canada
– everything you need to know before going to study in Canada.
http://www.univcan.ca/universities/member-universities/
– a list of ALL Canadian universities with descriptions, websites, tuition costs, and even enrollment capacities!
http://www.scholarships-bourses.gc.ca/scholarships-bourses/non_can/opportunities-opportunites.aspx?lang=eng
– scholarships for international students to study and research in Canada.
http://www.studyincanada.com/Index.aspx?Redirect
– a useful site with a lot of information about studying in Canada.
https://www.canada.ca/en/services/immigration-citizenship.html
– to study in Canada, you need a study permit. How to obtain and extend it, and apply for a student work permit? This resource explains it all.
http://www.univcan.ca
– the association of colleges and universities of Canada.
https://cbie.ca/
– a site about Canadian education including information on scholarships, current events and updates in the education sector, and government support for international students.
http://lawstudents.ca/forums/
– the largest forum about law schools, legal education, and practice in Canada. You must register to ask questions and join discussions.
http://jeannesauve.org/about/
– Jeanne Sauvé Scholars Program.
http://www.vanier.gc.ca/en/home-accueil.html
– Vanier Canada Graduate Scholarships (Vanier CGS), approved by the Government of Canada, offer successful graduates (both Canadians and internationals) the opportunity to pursue graduate studies (Master’s, PhD) in humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, engineering, and medicine.
http://www.nserc-crsng.gc.ca/Students-Etudiants/PD-NP/Laboratories-Laboratoires/index_eng.asp
– Scholarship program for visits to Government of Canada laboratories.
http://www.fondationtrudeau.ca/en
– Trudeau Scholarships. Intended for postgraduate education in social sciences and humanities at Canadian universities. The program is of interest to those conducting research within one of four themes: human rights and dignity, responsible citizenship, Canada and the world, people and their natural environment. In total, 15 scholarships are awarded annually, for up to four years, with a value of up to 60,000 CAD per year. The application deadline is in December each year.
http://banting.fellowships-bourses.gc.ca
– Banting Postdoctoral Fellowships Program.
http://www.scholarships-bourses.gc.ca/scholarships-bourses/index.aspx?lang=eng
– Scholarships from the Government of Canada.
http://www.iccs-ciec.ca/index_en.php
– International Council for Canadian Studies.
http://canadainternational.gc.ca/ukraine/study-etudie/index.aspx?lang=ukr
– everything about studying in Canada.
List of resources for finding scholarships in Belgium
http://studyqa.com/
– the most prestigious study programs in Belgium! Convenient search by institution, field of study, and education level. Each program includes detailed information. Additionally, you can read about employment opportunities after graduation and student reviews.
http://www.belgium.be/en/education/
– a site for those curious about the language of instruction in Belgium, available scholarships and grants, recognition of foreign diplomas, and how the higher education system works.
http://www.enic-naric.net/index.aspx?c=Belgium
– how to get your foreign higher education diploma recognized in Belgium. All procedures and information about recognition centers in different regions are available here!
http://diplomatie.belgium.be/en/services/travel_to_belgium/Studeren_In_Belgie/
– a very useful resource that will help you choose a study location in Belgium and introduce you to the differences in education across the Flemish, Walloon, and German-speaking regions of the country.
http://www.studyinbelgium.be/en
– prepare for studying in Wallonia and Brussels with this portal! You’ll learn about different institutions and programs, admissions, exams, diploma recognition, student visas, tuition and living costs, health insurance, student jobs, and available scholarships and grants.
http://www.brussels.irisnet.be/education-and-training
– a resource about education in Wallonia and Brussels, offering information on all types of education, including second higher education, education for people with disabilities, as well as distance learning, language courses, diploma recognition, scholarships, and grants.
http://www.studyinflanders.be/
– an overview of universities, colleges, and study programs in Flanders. Here you can learn about admission requirements, scholarship programs, visas, insurance, expenses, and everything else you should consider before starting your studies.
http://www.highereducation.be/home
– excellent search for education programs in Flanders by keywords, name, specialization, type, language, and study duration. Also provides information about residence permits and visas, diploma recognition, health insurance, admission conditions, grading systems, scholarships, tuition, and living costs in Flanders.
https://www.vlaanderen.be/en/studying
– a site with useful articles about education, tips on good Dutch language courses, grants, and recognition of Flemish diplomas abroad.
http://www.research.be/
– a Belgian portal for research and innovation, designed to facilitate communication between students, PhD candidates, and professors, and to provide you with information about ongoing research projects and institutes, as well as funding sources for your future doctoral research.
There are also a number of resources and websites for searching for scholarships in other countries.

https://studyinaustria.at/
